newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-News Corp in alliance with EchoStar.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-News Corp in alliance with EchoStar.

text.p: News Corp Ltd said on Tuesday it had formed a direct broadcast satellite alliance with U.S. satellite broadcaster EchoStar Communications Corp and would contribute assets of US$1 billion from its American Sky Broadcasting (AskyB) unit to the joint venture.

News Corp said it would hold 50 percent of the equity of EchoStar as a result of the deal and MCI Communications Corp would hold 20 percent of News Corp's 50 percent interest or 10 percent of EchoStar.
News Corp said the alliance was designed to mount vigorous competition in the U.S. subscription television market.
"Jointly we will create a dynamic and promising new competitive force in the subscription marketplace," News Corp chairman and chief executive Rupert Murdoch said in a statement.

The company said EchoStar's direct broadcast satellite (DBS) business would continue to be headquartered in Englewood, Colorado and would operate under the trade name, Sky, which is utilised by News Corp's DBS services around the world.
EchoStar was expected to spin off certain assets, including its manufacturing and international businesses, to existing shareholders, News Corp said.

"The new Sky service is expected to include seven satellites, more than 500 channels advanced technology, retransmission of local TV stations in markets representing more than 75 percent of all U.S. television households, low consumer entry cost and superior customer service," News Corp said.
News Corp said the EchoStar's chief executive, Charles Ergen, would retain his position while Murdoch would serve as EchoStar's chairman.

News Corp said chief executive of AskyB, Preston Padden had been appointed as the president of the company's worldwide satellite operations and in this capacity, Padden together with Murdoch, would oversee News Corp's investment in EchoStar.
Padden would report to Chase Carey, co-chief operating officer of News Corp.
The company said Carl Vogel would serve as executive vice president of EchoStar and Paul Haggerty, currently the chief financial officer of AskyB, would become EchoStar's new chief financial officer.
